newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says mulls Taiwan VP transit visa request.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says mulls Taiwan VP transit visa request.

text.p: The United States is considering a transit visa request for Taiwan's Vice President Lien Chan, the State Department said on Friday.
Lien has requested permission to transit on his way to the Jan. 10 inauguration in Managua of Nicaraguan President-elect Arnoldo Aleman, State Department spokesman John Dinger said.
He noted there was a precedent for transit permission for senior Taiwanese leaders for their safety, comfort and convenience and said such visas were granted on a case-by-case basis.
The United States downgraded its ties with Taiwan after it established formal diplomatic relations with China in 1979.

U.S.-Chinese ties went into a nosedive from which they have only recently begun to recover after Washington let Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui enter the United States to attend a college reunion in June 1995.
